## Public Rate-Limit Client Identity Hardening - 2026-07-11

Status: Implemented and fully verified.

### What Changed

- Public rate-limit identity now prefers Vercel's canonical `x-vercel-forwarded-for` request header.
- Only valid IPv4 or IPv6 values can become durable rate-limit bucket identities; arbitrary strings and oversized attacker-controlled labels collapse to `unknown`.
- When `VERCEL=1`, a missing or malformed canonical Vercel identity fails closed instead of trusting fallback forwarded headers.
- Validated `x-forwarded-for` and `x-real-ip` fallback remains available for local or self-hosted environments.
- Durable keys now contain a versioned, route-separated SHA-256 digest instead of the validated raw address text.
- The digest is a data-minimization boundary, not an anonymity claim; existing retention and access controls still apply to rate-limit rows.
- Existing public intake, demo request, verified notification, and family document upload limits, durable RPC behavior, `Retry-After` responses, and pre-body-parsing order remain unchanged.

Vercel documents `x-vercel-forwarded-for` as equivalent to its client IP view and specifically useful when `x-forwarded-for` may be overwritten by another proxy: `https://vercel.com/docs/headers/request-headers#x-vercel-forwarded-for`.

### What Changed In Plain English

Attackers can no longer invent arbitrary text values to obtain fresh rate-limit buckets. On Vercel, Vinea uses the platform's canonical client-address signal; malformed or missing identity is grouped into one conservative bucket. The durable table receives an opaque digest rather than the readable address.

## AI Family And Cross-Parish Safety Contract Prepared

Status: Completed as a non-runtime AI safety implementation phase. Vinea now has a safety check for future AI retrieval that says AI can only be considered for staff-internal use when the staff member, parish, request, sources, audit metadata, and review status all line up. It also says family portal pages should not receive AI output, and any public-facing denial should stay generic. This does not change the live app yet.

### Why This Matters

Before Vinea expands AI, it needs guardrails that prevent wrong-parish data and family-facing leaks. This contract gives future AI work a tested doorway so broader retrieval cannot quietly bypass parish scope, membership scope, or family portal boundaries.

Now Vinea trusts the staff membership check for access and uses a blank parish name fallback when the name is not visible. This fixes the shared QA request-detail/document smoke test with the parish switcher cookie turned on.

The active parish cookie is the foundation for parish switcher behavior. This fix keeps access strict without making request detail and document routes depend on extra parish display visibility that RLS may intentionally hide.

## Household Duplicate Merge Active-Parish Write Context

Status: Implemented. No production public intake routing was enabled, no migrations were applied, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Updated `app/api/households/duplicates/route.ts` so Household duplicate merge POST writes resolve parish scope through `resolveStaffWriteParishContext()`.
- When an active parish cookie is present, Household duplicate merge writes now require membership authorization for that selected parish.
- When no active parish cookie is present, Household duplicate merge writes preserve the explicit `primary_parish_id()` compatibility fallback.
- Continued filtering all Household merge updates, deletes, member transfers, and audit attribution by the resolved parish id.
- Updated `lib/server/householdDuplicatesRoute.test.ts` with focused POST tests for active parish writes, no-cookie fallback, unauthorized active parish denial, and no direct legacy primary parish helper call.
- Updated `docs/MULTI_PARISH_REMAINING_PATHS_INVENTORY.md` and its validation test so both People and Household duplicate merge writes are marked active-parish aware.

### What Changed Plain English

Before this update, the Household duplicate merge action still used the older single-parish lookup. Now, if a staff member has selected an active parish, Vinea checks that the staff member is allowed to write to that parish before merging duplicate households. If no parish has been selected yet, the old single-parish behavior still works for compatibility.

### Why This Matters

Household merges can delete one household and move members to another household. That is a sensitive write action. Making the Household merge path respect the selected authorized parish closes the last duplicate-merge write gap before Vinea moves toward disposable operational RLS validation.

## Public Intake Runtime Safe QA Route Wiring

Status: Implemented and verified for safe QA wiring only. `/api/intake` now calls the prepared runtime gate, route-signal helper, parish-scope adapter, and public parish-scope resolver. Runtime routing remains disabled by default unless both exact safe QA flags are set. With flags off, the adapter preserves legacy primary-parish request creation. No migrations were added or applied, production/shared QA data was not touched, runtime flags were not enabled, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Updated `app/api/intake/route.ts` so public intake request creation now:
  - runs durable rate limiting before body parsing
  - parses and validates the request body before parish-scope resolution
  - calls `getPublicIntakeRoutingRuntimeGate()`
  - extracts route signals from request URL, headers, and body
  - resolves parish scope through `resolvePublicIntakeRequestParishScopeForFutureRuntime()`
  - preserves `primaryParishId(admin)` as the flag-off legacy fallback
  - resolves token/domain/slug routing only when the exact safe QA flags are enabled
  - resolves parish scope before creating parishioner or request rows
  - merges `...scope.auditMetadata` into `public_intake.created`
  - keeps partial cleanup behavior intact
- Added `lib/server/publicIntakeRuntimeRouteWiring.test.ts`.
- Updated public intake routing strategy, guard, adapter, acceptance, approval, and checklist docs/tests from planning-only to safe-QA-wired status.
- Public responses for unexpected server errors now use the generic `Could not submit request.` message instead of returning raw exception messages.

### What Changed Plain English

Vinea’s public form backend now has the parish-routing switch installed, but the switch is off by default. If the switch is off, public forms keep going to the same legacy parish as before. If the exact safe QA flags are turned on in a test environment, Vinea can route a public form by token, verified domain, or parish slug so the team can prove it works before production.

### Why This Matters

This is the first real runtime step toward multi-parish public intake. It lets Vinea test parish-specific public forms safely while protecting current public forms and keeping production behavior unchanged.

## Public Intake Routing Domain Ownership Verification

Status: Implemented and verified in code/tests. Added staff-only domain ownership verification for public intake routing domains. Runtime public intake routing was not wired, production/shared QA data was not touched, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Added `20260626103000_public_intake_domain_verification.sql`.
- Added additive DNS verification metadata columns to `parish_public_intake_domains`:
  - `verification_token`

- Updated `/api/parish/public-intake-routing` so new domains receive a DNS TXT verification challenge.
- Added staff-only domain verification actions:
  - `Verify DNS`
  - `Reset verification token`
- Verification checks DNS TXT records for the expected Vinea value and records safe pass/fail metadata.
- Verification reset clears `verified_at`, generates a new TXT challenge, and keeps the domain staff-visible.
- Added audit events:
  - `public_intake_domain.verification_reset`
  - `public_intake_domain.verified`
  - `public_intake_domain.verification_failed`
- Updated Parish Settings to show the DNS TXT record name/value, last checked time, verification error, and verification buttons.
- Updated `/api/health` schema readiness to require the new domain verification metadata columns.
- Updated the manual QA checklist to include DNS verification and reset cases.
- Kept runtime public intake routing unwired.

### What Changed Plain English

Staff can now prove that a parish controls a domain before Vinea ever uses that domain for public forms. Vinea gives staff a DNS TXT record to add, checks whether the record exists, and records whether verification passed or is still pending. This prepares Vinea for safer parish-specific public intake links without changing what families see today.

### Why This Matters

Domain routing is security-sensitive. Without ownership verification, one parish could accidentally or maliciously claim a domain it does not control. This phase adds the safety foundation needed before turning on any family-facing domain routing.

## Public Intake Routing Token Management

Status: Implemented and verified. Parish settings now supports staff-only public intake token management for the active parish. Staff can create a token, see the raw token exactly once in the creation response, and activate/deactivate existing tokens. The database stores only `token_hash`; normal metadata loading does not return raw tokens or token hashes. Runtime public intake routing was not wired, no migrations were added or applied, production and shared QA were not modified, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Added staff-only token creation through `POST /api/parish/public-intake-routing`.
- Generated public intake tokens server-side using cryptographically secure random bytes.
- Stored only a SHA-256 token hash in `parish_public_intake_tokens.token_hash`.
- Returned the raw token only once in the token creation response.
- Added staff-only token activate/deactivate through `PATCH /api/parish/public-intake-routing`.
- Scoped token writes through the active parish cookie and `resolveStaffWriteParishContext`.
- Preserved explicit primary parish compatibility fallback only when no active parish cookie exists.
- Validated token labels, supported request types, and optional expiration dates.
- Added audit events:
  - `public_intake_token.created`
  - `public_intake_token.updated`
- Added a public token creation form to `/dashboard/settings`.
- Added one-time token display copy explaining that Vinea only shows the full token once.
- Added activate/deactivate buttons for configured public tokens.
- Kept runtime public intake routing unwired.

### What Changed Plain English

Staff can now create secure public form tokens for future parish-specific intake links. When a token is created, Vinea shows the full token one time so staff can save it. After that, Vinea only stores a protected fingerprint of the token, not the token itself.

### Why This Matters

Public tokens are sensitive because they may eventually help route family-facing forms to the right parish. This phase gives Vinea a safer token-management foundation before turning any public routing live. It also keeps an audit trail of who created or changed tokens.

## Public Intake Routing Schema Promotion

Status: Implemented and verified as a schema-only promotion. The public intake parish routing migration candidate was promoted into `supabase/migrations` as `20260625193000_public_intake_parish_routing.sql`, and `/api/health` now checks for the promoted schema objects. Runtime public intake routing was not wired, public forms still use the existing legacy intake behavior, production and shared QA databases were not touched by this coding phase, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Added `supabase/migrations/20260625193000_public_intake_parish_routing.sql`.
- Added parish public-routing columns: `public_slug`, `public_display_name`, and `public_intake_enabled`.
- Added staff-managed public intake routing tables:
  - `parish_public_intake_domains`
  - `parish_public_intake_tokens`
- Kept routing tables protected by RLS with authenticated staff policies scoped through `is_authorized_for_parish(parish_id)`.
- Added no anonymous direct-write policies.
- Updated `/api/health` schema readiness checks for:
  - `public intake parish routing columns`
  - `public intake domain routing table`
  - `public intake token routing table`
- Kept rollback reference at `docs/sql/public_intake_parish_routing_rollback_draft.sql`.
- Updated public intake routing docs and tests from "not promoted yet" to "schema promoted, runtime routing still unwired."

### What Changed Plain English

Vinea now has the database foundation needed for future multi-parish public intake routing. This means the database can store a parish's public form slug, approved web domains, and secure form tokens. Public forms do not use this yet; families will still experience the same intake forms as before until a later approved phase connects the routing logic.

### Why This Matters

This is a major step toward multi-parish and diocesan readiness. It lets Vinea prepare for parish-specific public forms without rushing the riskier part: changing how live public requests are routed. Parish staff gain a safer path toward using Vinea across parish clusters, while Vinea gains an important Catholic-specific enterprise foundation.

## Phase 3: Request Detail Workflow Step System

## Phase 4: Request Document Support

Status: Implemented and verified.

### What Changed

- Added private Supabase Storage bucket setup for `request-documents`.
- Added `request_documents` with staff-only RLS scoped by `is_authorized_staff()`, `primary_parish_id()`, and `request_belongs_to_primary_parish(request_id)`.
- Documents can optionally be linked to a request-specific `request_workflow_steps` row.
- Added staff-protected document APIs:
  - `GET /api/requests/[id]/documents` lists documents for a scoped request.
  - `POST /api/requests/[id]/documents` uploads a document server-side, writes metadata, and records an audit event.
  - `GET /api/requests/[id]/documents/[documentId]` returns a short-lived signed download URL.
  - `PATCH /api/requests/[id]/documents/[documentId]` approves or rejects a document with an optional review note.
- Added a request-detail "Request documents" section under Workflow steps.
- Staff can upload documents, select a document type, tie a document to a workflow step, open the private file, and approve or reject it.
- Added audit event labels for document uploads and reviews.
- Added focused unit tests for document filename sanitization, status normalization, row normalization, and file-size formatting.

### How To Test

1. Apply Supabase migrations through the normal project migration process.
2. Open a Baptism, Wedding, Funeral, or OCIA request detail page as authorized staff.
3. Go to the Scheduling tab and find Workflow steps.
4. In Request documents, upload a small PDF or image.
5. Optionally choose a workflow step before uploading.
6. Confirm the document appears in the list with `Pending review`.
7. Click Open and verify the document opens through a signed URL.
8. Add an optional review note and approve or reject the document.
9. Check request activity or `/dashboard/admin/audit-log` for document upload and review events.
10. Run:

```bash
npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run build
npm.cmd run lint
```

### Known Risks

- This phase is staff-facing only. Families cannot upload documents yet; that remains Phase 5.
- Required document rules are not yet modeled at the workflow-template level. Staff can tie uploaded files to workflow steps, but Vinea does not yet auto-block completion based on missing or rejected documents.
- Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB in the server route, but file type restrictions are intentionally broad for parish paperwork.
- Storage access is private and mediated by server-generated signed URLs; direct browser storage policies are not opened in this phase.

## Phase 5: Secure-Token Family Document Portal

Status: Implemented and verified.

### What Changed

- Added `request_portal_tokens` for revocable, expiring family document portal links.
- Raw family portal tokens are never stored; only SHA-256 token hashes are persisted.
- `request_portal_tokens` has RLS enabled with no anon/authenticated policies. Access is mediated through server-side routes after staff authorization or token validation.
- Added `POST /api/requests/[id]/portal-token` so authorized staff can generate a 30-day family upload link from the request detail document panel.
- Added `/family/request/[token]` as a family-facing document portal.
- Added `POST /api/family/request-portal/[token]/documents` for token-based family uploads.
- Family uploads go into the private `request-documents` bucket and create `request_documents` rows with `pending_review` status.
- The family portal exposes only:
  - Parish name.
  - Basic request label, submitted contact name, request type, child name when present, and link expiration.
  - Required workflow steps where `owner_type = 'family'`.
  - Redacted document metadata tied to those required family-owned workflow steps.
- The family portal does not expose internal notes, staff-only request fields, communication history, AI notes, audit logs, assignment data, private storage paths, staff review notes, or arbitrary documents not tied to family-facing workflow steps.
- Staff can copy the generated family upload link from the Request documents panel.
- Added audit labels for family portal link creation and family document uploads.
- Added focused tests to ensure family portal document metadata is filtered to family-facing workflow steps and staff-only document fields are redacted.

### How To Test

1. Apply Supabase migrations through the normal project migration process.
2. Open a Baptism, Wedding, Funeral, or OCIA request detail page as authorized staff.
3. Ensure the request has at least one required workflow step owned by `Family`.
4. Go to the Scheduling tab and find Request documents.
5. Click `Create family upload link`.
6. Open the generated `/family/request/[token]` link in a new browser session or private window.
7. Confirm the page shows only basic request context and required family-owned workflow steps.
8. Upload a small PDF or image for one requested document.
9. Return to the staff request detail page and confirm the document appears as `Pending review`.
10. Approve or reject the uploaded document from the staff UI.
11. Confirm invalid or expired token links show the generic unavailable-link message.
12. Run:

```bash
npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run build
npm.cmd run lint
```

### Known Risks

- Portal links are bearer tokens. Anyone with the link can upload documents until expiration or revocation in the database.
- Staff UI can create links, but revocation and link history are not exposed in the UI yet.
- Required document rules are still inferred from required family-owned workflow steps; there is no separate document-requirement template model yet.
- The portal intentionally does not expose staff review notes to families, even for rejected documents, because Phase 4 review notes may contain internal context.
- The portal does not yet send automated email invitations or upload confirmations.

### Verification

- `npm.cmd test` passed: 39 test files, 150 tests.
- `npm.cmd run build` passed on Next.js 16.2.2.
- `npm.cmd run lint` passed with 58 existing warnings and 0 errors.
- Build still reports the existing Next.js middleware deprecation warning; Phase 5 did not change middleware/proxy behavior.

The current workspace cannot apply DDL migrations to the QA Supabase database. Supabase service-role API access can query and mutate rows, but it cannot create tables, alter columns, create RLS policies, create functions, or apply migration SQL without one of:

- A direct Postgres connection string (`SUPABASE_DB_URL` / `DATABASE_URL`) usable by `psql`.
- Supabase CLI installed and authenticated to the target QA project.
- A Supabase access token/project ref workflow that can run migrations through the official CLI.
- A pre-existing privileged SQL execution RPC in the QA database.

### QA Impact

```bash

```

or install/authenticate the Supabase CLI for this project, then rerun the migration and authenticated QA prompt.

## Durable Public Intake Rate Limiting

Status: Implemented.

### What Changed

- Added a durable `rate_limit_buckets` table for server-side abuse protection on public intake routes.
- Added `check_public_intake_rate_limit(key, limit, window_seconds)` as an atomic Supabase RPC.
- Kept `rate_limit_buckets` RLS-enabled with no anon/authenticated policies; access is mediated through service-role route handlers.
- Updated `/api/intake` to use the durable rate-limit RPC before creating parishioners, requests, checklist rows, workflow steps, or audit events.
- Preserved the existing in-memory limiter only as a rollout fallback when the new RPC/table has not been deployed yet.
- Added `/api/health` schema readiness checks for the rate-limit table and RPC.
- Added focused tests for durable allow/block behavior, rollout fallback, unexpected RPC errors, and schema readiness coverage.

### Why This Was The Next Safe Phase

- Workflow Templates + Document Portal is complete through Phase 5 and migration parity has been restored.
- The roadmap/source-of-truth identifies in-memory rate limiting as a known production security limitation.
- Public intake is the main unauthenticated doorway into Vinea. Durable rate limiting protects Baptism, Funeral, Wedding, OCIA, and Join Parish forms without changing staff workflows.
- This is a high-ROI readiness foundation that is safer than jumping directly into broad multi-parish tenancy.

### How To Test

1. Apply repository Supabase migrations to QA or a disposable Supabase project.
2. Confirm `/api/health` reports `checks.schema: true`.
3. Submit a normal public intake form and confirm the request is created.
4. Submit more than eight public intake requests from the same client IP within one minute.
5. Confirm the ninth submission returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`.
6. Confirm authenticated staff dashboard access and request processing are unchanged.
7. Run:

```bash
npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run build
npm.cmd run lint
```

### Known Risks

- Until the new migration is applied, `/api/intake` intentionally falls back to the previous in-memory limiter so deployments do not break during rollout.
- Rate limiting keys are based on forwarded IP headers. In production, trusted proxy/header configuration still matters.
- The current limit remains eight submissions per minute per client IP; parishes with unusual shared-network behavior may need tuning after pilot feedback.

### Verification

- `npm.cmd test` passed: 44 test files, 165 tests.
- `npm.cmd run build` passed on Next.js 16.2.2.
- `npm.cmd run lint` passed with 58 existing warnings and 0 errors.

## Durable Public Intake Rate Limiting QA Migration Attempt

Status: Blocked before migration application.

### What Changed

- Re-read the roadmap/source-of-truth and build status after the durable public intake rate-limiting implementation.
- Verified the active Codex toolset still does not expose callable Supabase MCP tools.
- Verified `npx.cmd supabase` is available and reports Supabase CLI `2.107.0`.
- Verified the CLI is not authenticated in this environment:
  - `supabase projects list` returns `Access token not provided`.
  - `supabase migration list --linked` returns `Cannot find project ref`.
- Verified the QA Supabase project is missing the new durable rate-limit objects:
  - `public.rate_limit_buckets`
  - `public.check_public_intake_rate_limit(text, integer, integer)`
- Verified the QA database does not expose a privileged SQL execution RPC such as `exec_sql`, `execute_sql`, `run_sql`, or `sql`.

### Blocker

The current session can query QA through the app's service-role Supabase client, but it cannot apply DDL migrations. Applying `20260622160000_public_intake_rate_limits.sql` requires one of:

- A direct Postgres connection string passed to:

```bash
npx.cmd supabase db push --db-url "postgresql://..."
```

- Or an authenticated Supabase CLI session with project link details:

```bash
npx.cmd supabase login
npx.cmd supabase link --project-ref gnfomgsuottcuueasfvi --password "..."
npx.cmd supabase db push --linked
```

- Or callable Supabase MCP SQL/migration tools in the active Codex session.

### QA Impact

- `/api/health` is expected to report `checks.schema: false` until the new migration is applied.
- Public intake still has the rollout fallback to the previous in-memory limiter, so normal intake should not break before migration application.
- The requested durable 429 behavior cannot be truthfully verified until the database migration is applied.

### Next Highest-Priority Unfinished Roadmap Item

After durable rate-limit QA is unblocked and verified, the next highest-priority unfinished item is true multi-parish/diocesan tenancy foundation.

Reasoning:

- The current V1 `primary_parish_id()` model is repeatedly documented as the largest production/security limitation.
- It affects RLS, staff authorization, parish data isolation, diocesan pilots, and customer acquisition beyond a single pilot parish.
- It is more foundational than broader certificates, payment/stipend expansion, richer email templates, or calendar conflict detection.

Recommended next safe phase:

- Design and implement the first tenant-membership foundation only:
  - Add `parish_memberships` or equivalent user-to-parish membership table.
  - Add helper functions that resolve parish scope from the authenticated user.
  - Keep existing `primary_parish_id()` behavior as a compatibility fallback.
  - Do not migrate all RLS policies in one step.

### How To Test After Credentials Are Available

1. Apply the migration to QA.
2. Start the app:

```bash
npm.cmd run dev -- -p 3000
```

3. Open `/api/health` and confirm `ok: true` and `checks.schema: true`.
4. Submit one safe public intake request and confirm it creates normally.
5. Submit more than eight public intake requests from the same client IP within one minute and confirm the ninth returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`.
6. Confirm staff dashboard request processing still works.

### Known Risks

- Running the rate-limit stress test creates safe disposable QA intake records unless a dedicated cleanup script is used afterward.
- Rate limiting keys depend on trusted forwarded IP headers; production proxy behavior should be verified before launch.

## Staff Write Parish Context Helper

Status: Implemented and verified.

### What Changed

- Added `lib/server/staffWriteParishContext.ts`.
- Added `resolveStaffWriteParishContext()` as a server-only write-safety helper for future multi-parish write migrations.
- The helper requires membership authorization by default.
- For writes without an explicit parish id, the helper resolves `current_staff_primary_parish_id()`.
- For writes with an explicit parish id, the helper verifies `is_authorized_for_parish(p_parish_id)`.
- `primary_parish_id()` compatibility fallback is available only when callers explicitly pass `allowPrimaryParishFallback: true`.
- Fallback cannot authorize a requested parish id that differs from the primary parish fallback.
- Did not wire operational write actions to the helper yet.
- Did not migrate operational table RLS.
- Added focused tests that verify:
  - Primary membership parish resolution.
  - Explicit requested parish authorization.
  - Denial when membership does not match.
  - Explicit legacy fallback behavior.
  - Fallback mismatch protection for requested parish writes.

## Active Staff Parish Context Resolver Foundation

Status: Implemented and verified.

### What Changed

- Added `lib/server/activeStaffParishContext.ts`.
- Added `resolveActiveStaffParishContext()` as a server-only foundation for a future parish switcher and active parish context UI.
- Added `ACTIVE_STAFF_PARISH_COOKIE = 'vinea_active_parish_id'` for future cookie-backed active parish selection.
- The resolver wraps the existing read-only `resolveStaffParishContext()` helper and chooses one safe `activeParishId`.
- If no parish is requested, the active parish defaults to the primary membership parish.
- If a requested parish belongs to the authenticated staff context, the requested parish becomes active.
- If a requested parish is stale, tampered with, or unauthorized, the resolver ignores it and falls back to the primary authorized parish with `ignoredRequestedParishReason`.
- Existing `primary_parish_id()` compatibility fallback remains available through the underlying read resolver for undeployed membership-foundation cases.
- Did not add visible parish switcher UI yet.
- Did not wire loaders, route handlers, or actions to active parish yet.
- Did not migrate operational table RLS.
- Added focused tests for:
  - Defaulting active parish to primary membership parish.
  - Honoring an authorized requested parish.
  - Ignoring an unauthorized requested parish.
  - Preserving primary-parish fallback when membership foundation is unavailable.
  - Cookie constant and requested parish normalization.

## Staff Document Active Parish Authorization

Status: Implemented and verified as the next safe multi-parish tenancy phase.

### What Changed

- Updated `lib/server/requestDocumentAccess.ts` so staff document authorization can use the active parish selected by the staff user.
- Staff document access now requires an exact membership-validated active parish match when the active parish cookie is present.
- Preserved explicit `primary_parish_id()` compatibility fallback only when no active parish cookie exists.
- Removed implicit primary-parish fallback from the document access helper default so future callers must opt into fallback deliberately.
- Updated these staff routes to pass the active parish cookie and authenticated staff Supabase client into document authorization:
  - `app/api/requests/[id]/documents/route.ts`
  - `app/api/requests/[id]/documents/[documentId]/route.ts`
  - `app/api/requests/[id]/portal-token/route.ts`
- Staff document list, upload, signed download, review, and family portal-token generation now follow the selected active parish at the application authorization layer.
- Added focused tests:
  - `lib/server/requestDocumentAccess.test.ts`
  - `lib/server/requestDocumentRouteAuthorization.test.ts`
- Updated `docs/MULTI_PARISH_REMAINING_PATHS_INVENTORY.md` so document authorization is marked complete and Workflow Template Settings API is now the highest-priority remaining path.

### What Changed Plain English

Before this update, document uploads, document review, and family portal link creation checked staff access against the oldest parish in the database. That was acceptable for one parish, but not for a staff user who can switch between multiple parishes. Now those document actions respect the parish the staff user has selected, and Vinea verifies that the staff user is actually allowed to access that parish. This helps parish staff work in the correct parish context and reduces the risk of viewing or changing another parish's request documents by mistake. No action is required unless you want to manually QA document upload/review with a multi-parish test staff account.

### How To Test

1. Sign in as a staff user with access to more than one parish.
2. Switch the active parish.
3. Open a request in that parish.
4. Verify staff can list documents, upload a document, open a signed download URL, approve/reject a document, and generate a family portal link.
5. Switch to a different parish and verify the previous parish's request documents are not accessible through staff document routes.
6. Run:

```bash
npm.cmd test -- lib/server/requestDocumentAccess.test.ts lib/server/requestDocumentRouteAuthorization.test.ts
npm.cmd test -- --reporter=dot
npm.cmd run build
npm.cmd run lint
```

### Known Risks

- Operational table RLS was intentionally not changed in this phase.
- The document routes still use the service-role client for document reads/writes after the staff authorization gate, matching the existing architecture.
- This phase improves application-layer authorization, but final database-level multi-parish enforcement still depends on the future membership-aware operational RLS migration.
- The active parish cookie path is stricter than the shared active-context read resolver: if the cookie is stale or unauthorized, document access fails closed instead of falling back to the primary parish.
- Build still reports the existing Next.js middleware deprecation warning.
- Lint still reports 58 existing warnings and 0 errors.

### Verification

- `npm.cmd test -- lib/server/requestDocumentAccess.test.ts lib/server/requestDocumentRouteAuthorization.test.ts` passed: 2 test files, 8 tests.
- `npm.cmd test -- --reporter=dot` passed: 80 test files, 291 tests.

## Request Audit Parish Context

## Public Intake Parish Scope Resolver

Status: Implemented and verified as the next safe multi-parish tenancy phase. This is a non-runtime helper only; it is intentionally not wired into `/api/intake` or public pages, no migrations were applied, and operational RLS was not changed.

### What Changed

- Added `lib/server/publicIntakeParishScope.ts`.
- Added `resolvePublicIntakeParishScope()` as a server-only helper for future public intake routing.
- Added a Supabase data-source adapter for future use after the routing schema is applied.
- The resolver uses explicit public routing signals in this order:
  - Signed public token.
  - Verified domain/hostname.
  - Parish slug.
  - Legacy public form path fallback.
- Staff active parish cookies are ignored by design.
- Added tests for:
  - Valid active token.
  - Expired token.
  - Token request-type mismatch.
  - Verified domain.
  - Unverified domain.
  - Enabled slug.
  - Disabled slug.
  - Legacy fallback.
  - New intake route without a valid signal.
  - Forged staff active parish cookie.
  - Guard that current public intake runtime files do not import the helper yet.
- Updated public intake routing strategy, QA validation, and multi-parish inventory docs.

### What Changed Plain English

Before this update, Vinea had a written plan for how future public intake links should choose the right parish. Now there is a small, tested helper that knows how that decision should work, but it is not connected to the live forms yet. This lets Vinea prove the routing rules safely before changing what families use today.

### How To Test

1. Confirm current public intake forms still use the existing routes.
2. Confirm `app/api/intake/route.ts` does not import `resolvePublicIntakeParishScope`.
